experiments.hypothesis: Baseline week — establishing initial metrics for the original Minesweeper game. No experiment is active; both variants point to the same V1 build.
experiments.changelog: Launched the original Minesweeper as V1 baseline.

experiments.hypothesis: Reducing the default game difficulty from a 16x16 grid with 40 mines to a 12x12 grid with 20 mines will increase average session value by at least 5% because easier games are likely to lead to a higher rate of games completed, which in turn could increase active play time per session and reduce frustration, especially for new players.
experiments.variantA: The control group experiences the current default Minesweeper game settings: a 16x16 grid with 40 mines.
experiments.variantB: The treatment group experiences a modified default Minesweeper game difficulty: a 12x12 grid with 20 mines.
experiments.changelog: Reducing the default game difficulty from a 16x16 grid with 40 mines to a 12x12 grid with 20 mines will increase average session value by at least 5% because easier games are likely to lead to a higher rate of games completed, which in turn could increase active play time per session and reduce frustration, especially for new players.

experiments.hypothesis: Slightly reducing the number of mines for the default 16x16 grid from 40 to 30 will increase average session value by at least 5% because a marginally easier game is likely to lead to a higher rate of game completions, which in turn could increase active play time per session and reduce frustration.
experiments.changelog: Slightly reducing the number of mines for the default 16x16 grid from 40 to 30 will increase average session value by at least 5% because a marginally easier game is likely to lead to a higher rate of game completions, which in turn could increase active play time per session and reduce frustration.
